notes: Takes calendar dates in and gives one out; it makes no requests. A host loads availability on monthChange and passes it back through enabledDates and dayMeta.
Month and weekday names and control labels are bundled for en, ar, ku and ru, so no locale file is fetched.

Rule precedence: range (min/max) → disabledDates → disabledWeekdays → not in enabledDates → isDateDisabled. The first rule that matches is the reason a day is blocked (data-reason on the cell). Rules only ever block: the allow-list never re-enables a day another rule blocked.

Disabled days are focusable but cannot be selected. Inside min/max, the arrow, Home/End and Page keys land on every day of the month, including disabled ones, which carry aria-disabled so a screen-reader user can discover them (the WAI-ARIA APG allows focusable disabled items in composite widgets). Enter and Space do nothing on them. Days of the neighbouring months and days outside min/max are never focused.
A min later than max is an empty range: every day is disabled, the month buttons, Today and the keyboard do not move, and the month stays where it opened unless the host sets month.

Appearance and colour scheme follow .shift form-appearances: every value resolves as --shift-calendar-x, then --shift-x, then the appearance, then the vanilla baseline, so host variables win in light and dark. The component never sets --shift-* itself.

Fonts: Nunito (vanilla, material, soft) or Manrope (sharp, minimal), with Noto Kufi Arabic first for ar and ku — all loaded by the package’s global script. Override with --shift-font-family and --shift-font-family-arabic.

The box never changes size: six rows always, a fixed header band, and the months and years views fill exactly the days view. Only another density (an appearance with a different cell size or gap) or another size resizes it.
Every movement — header roll, day carousel, view slide, year paging — runs on one clock: --shift-calendar-settle (or --shift-settle), 480ms by default; instant under prefers-reduced-motion.

notes: Takes the times of one day in and gives one out; it makes no requests. Times are HH:mm on a 24-hour clock whatever hourCycle shows.
Times sit in as many columns as fit (84px or wider at md), each at least 44px tall, so a narrow host gets fewer columns, never a scrollbar.

Selection follows Enter, Space or a click, not focus: arrows move focus only and pass over disabled times, so moving through the day with the keyboard never picks one. This is the documented difference from the WAI-ARIA radio group, where arrows also check.

When the times change, the outgoing grid fades while the incoming times rise one after another, and the height moves to the new row count on grid-template-rows. Loading shows skeletonCount placeholders the size of a time. Instant under prefers-reduced-motion.

Appearance and colour scheme follow .shift form-appearances: every value resolves as --shift-time-slots-x, then --shift-x, then the appearance, then the vanilla baseline. The component never sets --shift-* itself.
Fonts: Nunito (vanilla, material, soft) or Manrope (sharp, minimal), with Noto Kufi Arabic first for ar and ku, loaded by the package’s global script.

notes: One request per branch, from today: the endpoint’s booking delay counts from the request’s from date, so the field never pages forward. The days shown are whatever the response holds; days without times are dropped.

In a v1 form structure (type bookingCalendar) departmentPreference lists the departments it may book, in order (default ["showroom"]). A branch with none of them is not bookable: the field is disabled and its hint says so (booking locale branchUnavailable, or the node’s localization[lang].branchUnavailable). It never falls back to another department, whose hours would look bookable but be the wrong ones. The older bookingSlot and bookingDate fields still fall back to the branch’s first department.

Responses are cached per branch, department, brand, language and day for the page’s lifetime; errors are not cached and nothing retries on its own. A stale request is cancelled when the branch changes.
The submitted value and the slotChange detail are exactly branch-slot-picker’s: value YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm, detail { date, raw, value } with raw as the endpoint sent it.

States: idle (no branch yet), loading, ready, empty (no times at the branch) and error (with Try again). No day is chosen on load; the calendar opens on the month of the first open day. Reopening a day keeps the chosen time when that day has it, otherwise clears it.

The calendar owns its value. A value that is not one of the branch's times (a past booking, or one made elsewhere) is kept and labelled, never cleared by the calendar. The value is cleared only when branchId, departmentId or brandId changes after it was set: an id filled in for the first time is not a change, and neither is a host setting an id and the value in the same pass (a record loaded into the form). calendarApi and today changing keep it. A clear fires pickerChange with value "" and complete false.

Hosting with your own input: <shift-popover anchor="#input" placement="top" appearance="material" size="sm"> around <shift-booking-calendar appearance="material" size="sm">. Toggle the popover on the input's click, show pickerChange's label in the input and store its value; the popover closes itself when a time is picked. The calendar stays a separate element because the popover carries its content onto <body> and the calendar's views live in its own shadow root; shift-input type picker is the one-element field for pages that use shift-input.

Two views in one box: picking an open day switches from the days to that day's times, the header rolling from the month to the day and the content sliding toward the start (mirrored in RTL). Change date or Escape reverses it. The box keeps the calendar's size in both views and every state; a long day scrolls inside it. Nothing below the field moves: the status row has a fixed height and also carries the validation message.
Inside the field the calendar always fills the box; --shift-booking-calendar-max-inline-size and -min-inline-size set its width.
appearance, colorScheme and size pass to the calendar and the times; host --shift-* variables reach both, since they inherit.

props.description: Off (default): the panel stays anchored at every width. On: under 600px of viewport width it becomes a bottom sheet with a backdrop. Leave it off for pages shown inside an app’s webview.

props.name: placement
props.description: The preferred side. bottom (default): below the anchor, above when only above has room. top: above the anchor, below when only below has room. props.description: xs, sm, md (default), lg or xl. md equals no size.

notes: The content is slotted: the children of shift-popover move into a shift-popover-panel element that shift-portal appends to <body>, so no overflow or stacking context on the page clips them. Keep references to your content elements; do not look them up inside the popover after it loads. Children added later move too.

The panel receives the popover’s appearance, color-scheme and size attributes and its classes. It inherits nothing from where the popover sits, so set --shift-* variables on :root or on a class you give the popover.

Positioning, placement bottom (default): below the anchor, aligned to its inline start (its right edge in RTL, from the anchor’s computed direction); above when there is no room below. It never covers the anchor: when neither side has room it takes the larger side and caps its height to it, and the content scrolls inside the panel. Shifted sideways to stay 8px inside the viewport; re-placed on scroll of any ancestor, on resize and when the anchor or the content resizes. It never scrolls the page. When the anchor scrolls out of sight the panel closes. placement top is the mirror: above the anchor, below when only below has room, and the larger side when neither has.

With mobileSheet, under 600px of viewport width the panel is a bottom sheet whatever the placement: full width, at most 82dvh, sliding up from the bottom edge. Off by default, so the panel stays anchored at every width: a page inside an app’s webview fills only part of the screen, and a sheet there would sit at the bottom of the webview and dim only the webview.

Dismissal: pointer-down outside the panel and the anchor, Escape (focus returns to the anchor), Tab out of the panel (Shift+Tab from its first control returns to the anchor; Tab from its last moves to the control after the anchor), focus moving to any element that is neither the anchor nor a popover panel, a pickerChange with complete true from the content (a time or date picked in shift-booking-calendar or shift-calendar), and hide() from the content.

Focus on open: content with a setFocus() method (shift-calendar has one) is asked to focus itself; otherwise the first control in the content gets focus. show({ focus: false }) leaves focus where it is.
Wire a separate trigger button to toggle(): the pointer-down on it closes an open panel and the click that follows is ignored, so the button closes rather than reopens.

A non-modal popup (WAI-ARIA APG): the body-level shift-popover-panel element is the role=dialog and carries the id. On the anchor the popover sets aria-haspopup=dialog, and aria-controls pointing at that id whenever the anchor is in the document tree (an anchor inside a shadow root gets none, because an IDREF cannot cross the shadow boundary). It never sets or changes the anchor’s role: aria-expanded is set only when the anchor’s role allows it (a button, a combobox, or an element whose implicit role is button), so a foreign input that manages its own ARIA, such as a MudBlazor field, keeps it. shift-input’s own date input is a combobox. What the popover set is removed when the anchor changes.

The dialog always has a name: label; else, when the anchor is in the document tree and has a name of its own, aria-labelledby. For a form control (input, textarea, select) it points at the control’s name sources, never at the control, whose value would become the name: its aria-labelledby ids, else its <label> elements, except that when any label wraps the control the dialog gets the labels’ text as aria-label, with the control’s own contribution left out; a control with only aria-label gives the dialog that text, refreshed on every show(). Any other anchor, such as a button, is referenced itself. Ids the popover adds are removed again on cleanup. Otherwise the anchor’s aria-label or label text; else the localized “Pop-up”.

Several popovers can be open at once. show() on one closes another only when both share the same anchor, and focus moving into another popover’s panel does not close this one. A pointer-down outside a panel and its anchor still closes it.

Open grows and fades from the anchor edge, the sheet slides up; closing reverses. One duration, --shift-popover-settle (or --shift-settle), 320ms by default; instant under prefers-reduced-motion. The panel is position: fixed and never shifts the page layout.

The panel draws the chrome: surface, border, radius and panel shadow from the appearance. A shift-calendar in it draws none of its own and takes its size’s width; the page can still override both. minimal has no opaque surface or panel shadow in appearances.css; the panel fills them from the form-appearances guide until the shared tokens carry them.

notes: One element, one type at a time: text and date now. Each type is a module (types/<type>) that says how a value is shown, how typed text is read back, and what the type adds to the control; a new type adds a module, not a change to the field.

A form field (FormElement): subscribes to form under name, reports value through getValue(), resets to defaultValue, takes required, disabled and error state from the form, and adds a check to the field’s schema that fails while typed text is refused. Standalone it stands on isRequired, isDisabled and errorMessage.
Typed text is read on blur and Enter, never while typing; valueChange fires when the committed value changes.

type="date": value is YYYY-MM-DD or empty. The input shows it in format (default dd/MM/yyyy; tokens d, dd, M, MM, yyyy with any separators) and reads the format with any separators, eight digits in format order, or YYYY-MM-DD; Arabic-Indic digits are read as Latin. An impossible date, one outside min/max and one a rule closes leave the value empty and show a localized message; localization[language].format, .minMessage, .maxMessage ($minDate$, $maxDate$) and .unavailableMessage replace them.

type="date": the calendar button, Alt+ArrowDown and a click in the input (openOnControlClick) open a shift-popover holding shift-calendar, anchored to the input. A click leaves focus in the input so typing continues; the button and Alt+ArrowDown move focus to the selected day, else today, else the first day that can be chosen. Choosing a day writes the value and closes; Escape closes without changing it.

type="date": every shift-calendar prop passes through from one list (types/date/calendar-pass-through.ts): value, month, min, max, enabledDates, disabledDates, disabledWeekdays, isDateDisabled, dayMeta, today, highlightToday, weekStartsOn, numerals, disableViews, showToday, busy, disabled (from isDisabled), label, language, appearance, colorScheme, size.

The support line under the control is reserved in every state and holds the hint or the error, which cross-fade in it, so a message never moves anything below the field. A long message in a narrow field may wrap onto a second line.

Appearance, colour scheme, size and fonts as shift-calendar. The guide gives material and minimal no border: material is the filled text field (muted fill, square bottom corners, an underline that thickens and turns the focus colour on focus), minimal an underline with a muted label. These control tokens are local until appearances.css carries them. Classes on the field travel to its calendar panel.

notes: The day-strip counterpart of shift-calendar: the same inputs, the same dateChange, a horizontal row of day cards instead of a month grid. It makes no requests and knows nothing about branches or times.

Which days appear: min to max. When enabledDates is set and an end of the range is missing, that end is the first or last enabled date; with neither, 30 days from today (or the 30 days ending at max, when max is before today). A min later than max shows no days.
At most 366 days are rendered, counted from the first day of the range. Later days are not shown and cannot be selected; a value among them selects no card.

Rule precedence is shift-calendar’s, through the same library: range (min/max) → disabledDates → disabledWeekdays → not in enabledDates → isDateDisabled. Blocked days stay visible as disabled cards (data-reason names the rule); rules only ever block.

Semantics: a horizontal listbox of options (WAI-ARIA APG listbox), not a radiogroup, because the arrow keys move focus without selecting and Enter or Space selects; a radiogroup checks the radio the arrows land on. One card is in the tab order (roving tabindex): the selected day, else today, else the first open day. Disabled days are focusable with aria-disabled so they can be discovered.

Moving focus, setting value and the previous/next buttons scroll the strip only, never the page or an overflow: hidden ancestor. On first render the selected card is placed without animation; later changes scroll smoothly (instantly under prefers-reduced-motion). Scrolling snaps per card; touch swipe and trackpad scroll natively.
The previous and next buttons scroll by one visible page and are disabled at the ends. The edge fades grow with the distance scrolled, so they appear only where content continues.

The strip’s height never changes with selection, month labels, badges, highlightToday or the colour scheme; only another size, another density (appearance), the caption row, or the phone layout below a 600px viewport (roomier cards, as in the booking prototype) changes it.

Appearance and colour scheme follow .shift form-appearances: every value resolves as --shift-day-strip-x, then --shift-x, then the appearance, then the vanilla baseline, so host variables win in light and dark. The component never sets --shift-* itself.

Fonts: Nunito (vanilla, material, soft) or Manrope (sharp, minimal), with Noto Kufi Arabic first for ar and ku — all loaded by the package’s global script. Override with --shift-font-family and --shift-font-family-arabic.
